messages.content: Compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. Return JSON only. Use only what the text explicitly establishes. Do NOT invent an unmentioned release, retrieval, transfer, extra grip capacity, hidden hand position, or other transition. Treat one hand or foot as one exclusive physical resource for independent actions: if it is explicitly occupied and the next action needs that same hand/foot for a different independent task, that is CONFLICT unless the next text explicitly frees, transfers, repositions, or reuses the same held object for that action. COMPATIBLE = the next action follows physically from the established state. CONFLICT = the next action requires an occupied body part/object/state to be incompatible at the same time, or reverses an established state without an explicit transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text truly lacks enough physical information to decide. Do not rescue a contradiction by imagining a possible off-screen action.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Iris removes the right glove and drops it.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Iris is described one moment later as still wearing both gloves with no replacement.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. The previous action: "Iris removes the right glove and drops it." So after that, Iris has one glove removed (right glove) and dropped it on ground presumably. She still wearing left glove? It says she removes the right glove; so left remains.

Next micro-action: "Iris is described one moment later as still wearing both gloves with no replacement."

So at next action, she is wearing both gloves again. But we have not seen any action of replacing the removed glove or putting on a new one. So it's incompatible unless there's an implicit replacement? The instruction says: Use only what text explicitly establishes. No hidden hand position etc.

Thus after removal and drop, she has left glove only. Next micro-action states she's wearing both gloves again with no replacement. That is conflict because the right glove was removed and dropped; to be wearing it again requires a new action of putting on or picking up that same glove. Since none described, it's incompatible: CONFLICT.

Return JSON {"status":"CONFLICT"}
